correctness.rationale: For an n-periodic target y, an nt-periodic lift solves x_{i+d}-x_i=y_i on Z/(nt). The permutation i->i+d has gcd(nt,d)=g*gcd(t,b) disjoint cycles. Each cycle sum of the repeated target equals t/gcd(t,b) times the sum over one congruence class modulo g. Vanishing gives the asserted vector-order divisibility criterion; one initial value per cycle gives the exact kappa-power count. Prime valuations give the first feasible multiplier. F_y(kappa*b)=kappa^d proves the universal period bound. For primitive y, divisibility Möbius inversion yields all exact periods and t-fold orbit intersection. For uniform y, disjoint block sums are uniform independent mod kappa, and counting vector orders via the Jordan totient gives the exact full-target distribution. The delivered checker directly tested 81,090 preimage fibers, 1,484 primitive target cases and 95 all-output distributions; this is a finite cross-check, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 permutative-lift paper supplies the difference-code framework but studies minimality and unique ergodicity, not these all-length cyclic-fiber counts. Mariot et al. 2017 is strong prior art for algorithmic determination of preimage-period multiplicities, including linear bipermutive automata and finite rings; the present claim therefore excludes general computability or period-multiple observations. In inspected material, it does not state the uniform gcd/vector-order closed formula for every modulus, stride, and target, the minimum multiplier formula, or the unconditional Jordan-totient population law. This is an explicit arithmetic classification with independent derivation, not a new general algorithm. Historical formulations remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: The natural invariant is the shortest spatial period of a preimage of a periodic output under a finite permutative lifting code, for which a 2026 structural study supplies the finite-extension setting and a 2017 paper supplies only general algorithms in the relevant coverage. The single vector-order condition simultaneously determines the first possible period and every primitive preimage-orbit population across arbitrary moduli and strides. Its exact Jordan-totient distribution gives a robust all-length sampling statistic—including the sharp proportion kappa^{-g} of output words that retain the original period—which is not apparent from the general enumeration algorithm. This addresses a motivated finite-period classification and a natural random-output invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice; no broader generic algorithm or infinite-extension ergodicity is claimed.
